newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids lower.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids were lower Monday in response to a drop in futures prices, dealers said.
"Nothing's going on," a Montana wheat dealer said. "At these prices, there's no movement."
But a Minneapolis dealer said movement of wheat had been fairly active in Duluth.
"There's a lot of stuff for sale on the spot, but there's not much demand," the Minneapolis dealer said.
MGE July wheat futures settled 8-1/4 cents per bushel lower at $3.72, and other months were down 6-1/2 to nine cents.
Traders attributed the market's weakness to weekend rains in the northern U.S. Plains.

Meanwhile, the condition of North Dakota spring wheat declined during the week ended Sunday despite the arrival of beneficial rains, North Dakota's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
Forty-five percent of the state's spring wheat crop rated good or excellent, against 54 at that level last week.
